5.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Anacona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 5.1 through 5.7.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately 6:16

9.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting

David Siegrist – Mayor, City Council Member, Staff, and Public, Congratulations to our
newly elected Mayor, Ms. Jessica Ancona; our new City Council Woman Ms. Alma
Puente, and our re-elected City Council Woman, Ms. Victoria Martinez Muela. Your
campaigns were clean and fair. You set a great example for campaigning. Thank you,
Mayor Quintero and City Councilman Velasco for your many years of public service.
Many of us former members of our long defunct Sister Cities Commission are ready and
able to serve as volunteers again. New Mayor and City Council Members, please revive
all Commissions. We Sister Cities Commissioners worked hard raising thousands of
dollars by selling fireworks. When the Mayor terminated our Sister Cities Commission,
we left around Four Thousand dollars in our account. The moneys were restricted for
use ONLY by Sister cities Commissioners. We would like to know what happened to the
fruits of our hard labor. Rumor has it that a sitting City Council Member used much of the
money to pay his trip to Our Sister City, Zamora, Mexico. If true, he should be forced to
repay the money. Sister City Commissions are a mark of status and open up commercial
opportunities. I have had interest in forming a Sister City in Germany, South Korea, and
Indonesia. Sad to say, we started a wonderful link with Tomatlan, Mexico, El Monte lost
this link by terminating our Sister Cities. Please consider bringing our Sister Cities back.
Thank you.

Cosme Jimenez – I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate Councilwomen
Victoria Martinez and Alma Puente and our new Mayor Jessica Ancona. When it comes
to elections my conclusion is that people decided that our City and voted in favor of bring
back Victoria Martinez and Jessica Ancona as our new Mayor and I strongly agree.
Mayor Ancona you happen to be the third woman elected as Mayor in the history of our
City. It looks like we needed a woman to restore law and order at City Hall and as a
reminder City Hall belongs to the people and not the Mayor. Our City Mayor is a
desperate need of getting an improvement.  Our previous Mayor with two
Councilmembers voting yes all the time to me that is called a monarchy and forget about
the improvements because they are not going to work this way. We had eleven years of
monarchy with ex-Mayor Quintero and not only that but 25 years before he came over
for a total of 36 years all of this controlled by ex-Police Chiefs. Mayor Ancona you have
a big task ahead of you and I hope that Councilmembers Maria Morales and Alma
Puente represent the people that put them in office and not the ex-Mayor. Good luck to
you. Thank you.

Gabriel Ramirez – First of all I want to say congratulations to Vicky Martinez Muela for
being re-elected and congratulations to Alma Puente for being the new City
Councilmember and most importantly our new Mayor Madam Jessica Ancona. The
years of silencing have come to an end. The years of violations of the Brown Act and
the First Amendment silencing of all walks of life from women and men who are deeply
concerned about our City our issues that are happening the time has come now and now
a new fresh leadership has come to our City. There are still issues that need to be
addressed and I will continue to advocate and also our leaders to be working for the
people. This November has been an incredible mark of voter turnout a voice of the
community that decided that a new leadership with no longer of silencing and no more of
the bad deals that are not working for the community has come to an end. The status
quo has officially over and it is time now that we can continue back to get our community
back and for that thank you and have a great night.

  Scott Chamberlain - I represent the 3000 stakeholders of service providers, businesses,
  hospitals, schools and residents who want to prevent and end homelessness in the San
  Gabriel Valley. As the regional coordinator for the SGV, we help to educate
  communities, collaborate entities and advocate neighborhoods to address
  homelessness. We support any initiative that increases housing that is either bridge,
  permanent supportive or affordable housing the San Gabriel Valley, including the Project
  Homekey for M Motel. At the recent LAHSA homeless count presentation, one statistic
  stood out to me. It was that 2/3 of our unsheltered neighbors in LA County were on their
  first episode of homelessness, and 59% of those, cited economic hardship as their
  reason for falling into homelessness. This is so true in the suburban area, where normal
  people are falling into homelessness. It is a proven fact that housing, with supportive
  services, can solve the homelessness crisis. There are many services provided by LA
  County. However the land and the city support has been lacking for decades. Many of
  the concerns from neighbors are not true. Nice projects with staffing does not create
  eyesores or people hanging out on the corner. Bridge housing does not attract the
  homeless, as they are already in our community as neighbors. It is also cost beneficial
  for our city and county to get people the opportunities to get off the street, instead of
